podcast.body: A song from 2002, written by Deryck Whibley, whose publishing rights were sold to Harborview Equity Partners as part of Whibley's catalog sale. "Some 41 and still waiting from 2002."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Released in 2002, this song was later compared to an Italian single, "Almeno stavolta" by Nek, which came out in 2003. The two songs were found to have the "same melody line" but were likely "discovered totally independent," with everyone involved considered innocent. "Some 41 and Still Waiting released in 2002."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Released in 2002, this song was later noted for sharing the "same melody line" as Nek's Italian single "Almenos Alhorre," which came out a year later in 2003. Despite the similarity, both were considered independent discoveries. "Some 41 and Still Waiting released in 2002."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This song was a major hit for Sum 41. It gained attention on the internet for sounding very similar to an unnamed Italian recording from the mid to late 1990s. However, the similarity was ultimately attributed to an "unfortunate sonic coincidence" rather than plagiarism, given the simple, common structure of pop songs. "Major, major hit from some 41 still waiting."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
